sections.title: Communication Competence: Extracting Value in Key Organizational Interactions
sections.description: Often an organization can facilitate its own success by employing fundamental communication practices during value-latent interpersonal interactions. In this course we explore the direct relationship between competent communication and the ability to extract maximum value in most Key Organizational Interactions. Starting off on a personal development note and building off time-tested principles, participants will conduct their own communication skills assessment to determine their own communication strengths and identify specific areas for improvement. Qualities such as effective empathy and active listening are also explored. Moving into the organizational realm, together we define then locate those Key Organizational Interactions, both within and external to the organization, that significantly impact how that organization is perceived. We explore all the possible value points within these Key Organizational Interactions, how they tie into the organization's strategic objectives, and how to best approach them interpersonally. Non-DYNM students must complete a course permit request: https://www.sas.upenn.edu/lps/graduate/dynamics/course-permit

sections.title: Organizational Communication Essentials: Building Interpersonal Competence, Strategies & Practices
sections.description: This course explores the direct and indirect relationship between thoughtful communication practices and the ability to achieve organizational and interpersonal goals. Participants expand their communication repertoire while gaining insights into their organization’s communication culture. As course co-collaborators, they contribute personal insights and expertise throughout the semester, working with partners and teams as they become more agile and audience-focused communicators. They learn to recognize how context, status, and perfectionism influence all interactions, increasing the chances for successful communication. By the end of the course, students will be better equipped to communicate effectively with multiple audiences on various topics, with or without AI assistance. Non-Dynamics students: please include a brief job description in your Permissions Request.
